title: Thread divergence and memory layouts
status: reviewed and locally validated; independent round 2 ACCEPT
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: The 8-byte and 16-byte cache-line illustrations are hypothetical lecture models, rather than device cache-line specifications. No hardware transaction, cache, branch-efficiency or bank-conflict counters were collected.
The serialized-path and masked-loop equations are original simplified issue-work models qualified by compiler lowering and independent thread scheduling; they do not predict exact cycles.
Numba fragment is explicitly non-runnable explanatory API translation. No Numba package installation or device execution was performed. Version-string imports would not verify device execution.
The current CUDA Python latest page explicitly identifies a development-branch build; its description is not an installed-version guarantee.
Particle AoS/SoA event intervals exclude conversion; recurrence grouping excludes input permutation/gather cost; square transpose excludes general tail tiles.
Tiny transpose timings vary widely and overlap; measured samples do not establish a universal padding speedup or direct conflict penalty.

Source attribution repaired after R1: original slide pixels were inspected; the machine transcripts were not treated as proof of exact speech. No audio listening or independent spoken-word verification was performed. The CPU-allocation phrase is machine-transcript wording only; original allocation slides say GPU/device memory. Loop counts and byte capacity are stated as mathematical facts without unsupported speech-error allegations.

lecture_corrections.correction: Initial parity branch doubles even entries and increments odd ones; the later multiplier 2/3 expression is a different map. Odd input 5 yields 6 versus 15.
Comparison idx>=16 contributes 1 when true; the slide parenthesis reverses true and false. Evaluating a comparison and using ternary syntax do not themselves establish divergent control flow.
The original slide has the strict bound k<idx. It gives 31 iterations for lane 31. This is a mathematical clarification, not an independently verified error of speech.

Code and pictured indices use stride 2 despite the stride 3 parenthetical. The in-place gather can overlap another thread’s source reads. A generic safe transformation requires validated extents and separate buffers.

The original slide specifies 8-byte lines and 4-byte elements, so each line holds two elements. The assumed aligned packed 3x3 matrix has six row-line incidences but five distinct lines. A separate aligned vector occupies two more lines, giving seven unique cold lines. These counts are not elapsed cycles. No incorrect spoken byte count is independently alleged.
Separate allocations are not guaranteed adjacent. Concatenation in the diagrams is an explicit additional assumption.
Specify actual array type, allocation and strides instead of applying universal language or DataFrame layout claims. NumPy supports noncontiguous views.

The original slide explicitly describes uninitialized device memory and allocation on the GPU, consistent with the API. Only the machine transcript contains the CPU wording. No audio was independently checked and no spoken-error claim is made. The remaining API clarifications concern grid/gridsize tuples in 2D/3D and the distinction between host waiting and races inside a kernel.
